source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'SPD_FAN1_F~SPD_FAN16_F' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES passes the 16-channel expression as one literal record and cannot demonstrate individual readings. It does not decode `_F`, map physical fan assemblies and tach inputs, distinguish measured RPM from PWM target, or collect complete per-channel threshold/UI/freshness evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires suffix decoding and separate channels but interprets `_F` primarily as fault/status. Because the sensor prefix is `SPD`, values are readings with thresholds, and the immediately preceding paired family uses `_R`, V3.1 treats `_F` as presumptive front-rotor tachometer—not fault state—subject to the authoritative fan/controller specification.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 895/2291 accepts a literal range and output presence without defining front-rotor semantics, mapping sixteen tach channels or relating RPM to PWM/control state and UI evidence.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Wistron-BMC-00080-V003 separately requests dynamic threshold behavior, Wistron-BMC-00985-V002 separately covers list parity, and Wistron-BMC-00260-V002 uses a mismatched eight-entry Redfish fan array. The preceding `_R` row remains separate rear-rotor coverage and is only corroborative for assembly identity.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1057 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves suffixes; ED-34 treats rotor/fan/controller topology, tach scaling and RPM rules as readiness; ED-35 keeps this passive without PWM, fan removal, airflow or workload stimulus; ED-38 requires protected complete evidence, no clear/write/retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify `SPD_FAN1_F` through `SPD_FAN16_F`—presumptively the front-rotor tachometer channels of sixteen dual-rotor fan assemblies—are individually displayed in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct physical assembly/rotor identity, RPM, status and supported thresholds for the current fan-control state.
original_method: Confirm `_F` semantics, map each index to the physical fan assembly, front rotor, tach input and controller channel, then compare complete passive raw/UI RPM fields with duty-, zone- and operating-state-specific limits while recording PWM targets, inlet temperature, system load and airflow. Preserve fan policy and logs.
manual_activity: The thermal owner confirms F as front rotor or defines the actual suffix, maps all sixteen assemblies and controller tach inputs, and supplies state-dependent RPM limits. Automation can collect passive tach/controller/UI data; a human validates physical orientation and cooling context and owns the verdict. No fault injection, fan handling, PWM or airflow change is authorized.
required_inputs: Chassis/fan-board PN/revision, BMC/fan-controller build and authoritative `_F`/`_R` definitions
Fan1-16 physical assembly, thermal zone, airflow orientation, part/serial and dual-rotor construction map
Per-assembly front-rotor tach input, pulses per revolution, controller/bus/address/channel and scaling
Stable SDR and Dashboard/Server Health identities for all front channels
RPM units/rounding/tolerance, thresholds/hysteresis, state, polling and stale/absent rules
Current fan mode, PWM duty and target RPM per channel plus system load, inlet/ambient, altitude and airflow configuration
Acceptance for empty slots, stopped/missing front rotor, front/rear mismatch and degraded cooling
Validated protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, fan-controller, kernel or thermal logs; existing tach/fan events are relevant.
Do not issue `sensor get 'SPD_FAN1_F~SPD_FAN16_F'` as a wildcard. Enumerate sixteen exact channels.
Do not interpret F as fault merely from the letter or accept rear-rotor evidence as front coverage; confirm the controller/fan drawing and preserve the separate `_R` result.
Compare measured RPM with the contemporaneous controller target/duty and state-specific tolerance; do not judge a front rotor by an invariant absolute speed across fan modes.
Do not change fan mode/PWM, stop/remove/reseat a fan, obstruct airflow, start thermal load, alter thresholds or write the controller. These actions can compromise cooling.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the inaccessible Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped channels, stale RPM or raw/UI/controller disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate `_F`, sixteen fan/front-rotor/controller mappings, target, client, vendor specification and Script; build a front-rotor expectation matrix.
Read every front tach channel separately with full SDR/controller identity, RPM, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture the corresponding unchanged UI row.

Record simultaneous PWM duty/target RPM, fan mode, thermal zone, power/load, inlet/ambient and airflow, then calculate only the approved state-specific tolerance and front/rear correlation needed for identity or mismatch interpretation.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, PWM/fan/airflow/load/threshold/controller change, fault injection, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve F semantics and the sixteen physical assembly/front-rotor/tach-controller map.
Provide state-specific RPM/target tolerance, thresholds, mismatch/failure/absent and freshness rules; approve the protected read-only tool/Script.
Review all sixteen front channels independently and issue the formal verdict without treating rear rotors, a fault-state summary, a count or aggregate fan value as substitute coverage.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because the range expression is not an IPMI wildcard and one response cannot prove sixteen front-rotor channels. It omits suffix, physical rotor, controller/tach scaling and control-state context, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate the sixteen front channels, confirm physical rotor/controller identity, query each through protected read-only access, and correlate complete UI/controller RPM evidence with contemporaneous PWM targets and state-specific limits.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SPD_FAN1_F through SPD_FAN16_F, both WebUI paths, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or manipulating fans.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a sixteen-row front-rotor matrix keyed by physical fan assembly, rotor and controller tach channel, recording measured RPM with simultaneous PWM target/duty and thermal context, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with state-specific tolerances.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact sixteen-fan population, dual-rotor design and BMC/fan-controller/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/fan-board, BMC/fan-controller firmware, fan PN/revision, SDR/WebUI, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Mechanical airflow/fan map, dual-rotor fan specification, controller tach/PWM mapping and scaling, thermal-control policy, SDR/WebUI schema and Project recipe.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the compound range into sixteen physical front-rotor channels, corrects the prior fault-state interpretation and adds controller target/duty and operating-state evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static front-rotor RPM does not validate rear rotors, fan removal/stall detection, failover, PWM transitions, thermal response, airflow quantity or protection behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Suffix/rotor/controller map, state-specific RPM acceptance, passive synchronized timing, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Tach scaling depends on pulses per revolution, RPM changes with control mode and environment, and an alias or swapped front/rear channel can appear numerically plausible.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or fan-controller telemetry as an approved alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/channel/scaling and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate front-rotor identity, RPM, threshold, status and freshness coverage. Rear-rotor or aggregate fan evidence is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/fan-board and BMC/controller identity plus sixteen-row physical assembly/zone/orientation/PN/serial/front-rotor/tach-channel map
Controller/bus/address/channel, tach pulses-per-revolution/scaling and stable SDR/UI identity for every front channel
Complete separate raw readings with RPM, threshold capabilities/values, status and synchronized timestamps plus redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows
Simultaneous PWM duty/target, fan mode, load, inlet/ambient, altitude and airflow with per-channel state-specific tolerance and approved front/rear mismatch interpretation

Explicit empty/missing/stopped/swapped/stale/mismatched disposition, pinned Script/tool evidence, no-clear/no-PWM-or-fan-or-airflow-change/no-fault-injection/no-retry proof, final cooling/BMC health and engineer-owned front-channel verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The suffix and literal range are underdefined, but `SPD`, the paired `_R` family, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently support passive speed-display validation of sixteen `_F` channels. The exact front-rotor meaning remains a Project readiness input rather than a purpose conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The sixteen-channel fan-speed purpose is clear and the paired `_R` family makes a front-rotor interpretation plausible. Project fan documentation can confirm it and supply acceptance, so the review is not permanently BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, rear rotor, fault summary, aggregate fan value or tach-scaling error from being presented as sixteen front channels, and prevents fan/fault stimulus from being added to a passive Sensor Page test.
independent_technical_reasoning: A speed prefix plus paired F/R families is much stronger evidence for front/rear tach channels than for fault/redundant status. Each front RPM still needs physical rotor identity, controller scaling and simultaneous target/duty because normal speed varies with control state. This passive row cannot prove fault response or authorize fan manipulation.
